etymologies.etymologyHTML: 1601, verb attested 1622. Possibly borrowed from Middle French espraindre (“to press out, to wring”), from Latin exprimere, in which case cognate to express.

definitions.definition: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching; to overstrain, or stretch injuriously, but without luxation

quote.citation: 1963 June 8, Hare-Breadth Hurry, spoken by Bugs Bunny:
quote.text: Hi! I suppose you're expecting the Roadrunner! Well, he sprained a giblet cornering a sharp coive the other day, uh, so, uh, I'm standing in for him.

definitions.definition: The act or result of spraining; lameness caused by spraining
